data.narrative:
Noble Machines is a robotics and manufacturing startup founded by Wei Ding, Christopher McQuin, and Wenda Wang, operating in a sector with limited comparable valuations. The comp universe consists of one public peer (ticker 277810.KQ) and eight private robotics companies, including Divergent, Exotec, Locus Robotics, Generalist AI, and Bedrock Robotics.

The peer-median method is not applicable to this valuation. The analysis identified ten same-sector peers within Robotics & Manufacturing, but filtering by stage, adjacent stage, or similar valuation tier yielded fewer than three datapoints in any meaningful subcategory. Applying an all-sector median would introduce substantial noise given the heterogeneity of robotics business models, deployment timelines, and margin profiles. This methodological constraint reflects the frontier nature of the sector and the sparse availability of granular, stage-matched comparables.

Consequently, no triangulated valuation range can be supported by the data provided. Determining a defensible range for Noble Machines would require either: narrowing the comp set through direct fundraising data or revenue multiples from the five identified private peers; securing stage-specific context for the public comparable; or anchoring to transaction multiples from recent robotics M&A. Without such additional inputs, peer-based triangulation remains premature. Alternative methods—DCF, cost-of-capital approaches, or precedent financing rounds—would be required to establish a valuation framework.
